subject.title: fix(gateway): enforce plugin-ownership check in sessions.patch

question: Should plugin-runtime `sessions.patch` fail closed for every existing ownerless session row, or is an explicit upgrade path required for legacy plugin-created rows?
rationale: Source proves that ownership cannot be safely inferred for an existing ownerless row, while unconditional rejection may break previously working plugin-runtime mutations; repository policy requires maintainer intent for this security-versus-upgrade boundary.

options.title: Fail closed with owned creation
options.body: Reject legacy ownerless rows, stamp the authenticated plugin owner on newly created rows, and document the stricter upgrade behavior.

options.title: Add a narrow migration
options.body: Provide a verifiable doctor or owner-specific migration only for legacy rows whose plugin ownership can be established without allowing arbitrary adoption.

options.title: Preserve ownerless access
options.body: Continue allowing plugin-runtime patches to ownerless rows, accepting that multiple plugins may mutate the same unowned session.

recommendation.title: Fail closed with owned creation
recommendation.body: Reject legacy ownerless rows, stamp the authenticated plugin owner on newly created rows, and document the stricter upgrade behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the current plugin-runtime owner propagation and delete fence that define this security boundary.
